paper.title: Algorithm 863: L2WPMA, a Fortran 77 package for weighted least squares piecewise monotonic data approximation
paper.venue: ACM TOMS 33(1), Article 6 (Mar 2007); paper text not reached in this wake (ACM DL paywalled; the archive's Doc/INSTDE04.txt and Data/ are the source used)

code.commit: netlib TOMS archive 863.zip (scouted 2026-11-27, sha256 5947abcafb61ea258152d11ba98f8c81e28fcdfbcef832144362c7ca6d5f7657). Fortran 77 in 863/Fortran/Dp/ (driver1.f, rnd.f, src.f) and 863/Fortran/Sp/. Reference data and outputs in 863/Data/Appndx_B/ (XFWDAT input, WIVAPP, WPMAPP, WIAKN, WACTLG, RAPP_B). No RNG is needed for this driver.

claim.location: Shipped Appendix B of Doc/INSTDE04.txt (the printed output of DRIVER1 for the example data set), and the same numbers as the output file Data/Appndx_B/WIVAPP (column 2). The claim is the set of data indices of the extrema of the best monotonic approximation at the optimum, with KSECTN = 5 sections, for the 75-point data set Data/Appndx_B/XFWDAT and default weights (WFMODE 0).

reference.file: Data/Appndx_B/WIVAPP (shipped in 863.zip; Appendix B of Doc/INSTDE04.txt prints the same indices)

claim.metric: Data indices (ITHETA) of the extrema at the optimum, i.e. WIVAPP column 2 for increments 0..5, from DRIVER1 run on XFWDAT with 5 monotone sections
claim.paper_value: Indices 1, 8, 27, 46, 69, 75 as printed in INSTDE04.txt Appendix B. The paper text was not checked.

tolerance.basis: Fixed before any run. The values are integer data indices, so the only correct comparison is exact equality. A tolerance of 0 cannot hide a different optimum, and no rounding applies. Not loosened after any run.

cost.cpu_minutes_estimate: Under 1 minute (75 data points, one call of L2WPMA); plus a Fortran 77 compiler (gfortran is not on this host's PATH, so the rerun must install one).
cost.data_size: About 2 MB zip; the Appendix B data set is 75 records.
cost.data_licence: Not stated in the archive readme; the rerun should record the licence it finds.

why: The shipped Appendix B prints the optimum's extremum indices for a 75-point monotone fit, which the L2WPMA solver must compute from the weighted least squares problem, so the indices cannot be read off the code.
